classes.title: Invocation context capture or revalidation gap
classes.description: A Hub-affecting operation resolves mutable active/single-instance state at more than one time boundary without carrying and revalidating an immutable invocation token.

classes.title: Transaction commit-boundary validation gap
classes.description: Preconditions are checked before staging but not freshly revalidated immediately before an authoritative durable commit.

classes.title: Recovery reachability coupled to broken state
classes.description: A recovery operation requires successful validation of the state it is intended to bypass, replace or repair.

classes.title: State reachability changes across global/per-instance transition
classes.description: A layout or ownership transition changes which pending inputs/state are discoverable without migration, rejection or explicit fail-closed handling.

classes.title: Compatibility path diverges from canonical invariant
classes.description: A legacy/documented alias, restart path or compatibility entry point bypasses a safety/context contract enforced by the canonical path.

classes.title: Path or identity normalization assumption
classes.description: Filesystem path construction/comparison or instance identity handling trusts malformed, case-variant or insufficiently normalized input.

classes.title: Operation outcome or durability state is ambiguous
classes.description: Cancellation, pre-commit failure, durable commit, ambiguous write status and post-commit verification failure are not represented distinctly enough to preserve coherent recovery behavior.

classes.title: Filesystem publication semantics are non-atomic or destination-sensitive
classes.description: Directory/file publication can change semantics if the destination appears or changes between planning and publication instead of failing atomically on ambiguity.

classes.title: Qualification range identity is not validated
classes.description: A diff-driven qualification or risk-selection gate trusts caller-supplied base/head identities without proving a non-empty proper-ancestor range, allowing an empty, reversed or unrelated range to suppress required coverage.
